issues.title: Generic calendar suffix filtering includes disabled providers
issues.description: The getGenericCalendarSuffixes() method uses Object.keys(GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES) to iterate over all providers defined in the constant, including office365_calendar. However, getProviders() only returns ['google_calendar'], meaning Office365 is not actually enabled. This causes the subscription system to filter out Office365 calendar suffixes even when Office365 calendars shouldn't be processed at all. The filtering should only include suffixes for enabled providers by using this.getProviders() as in the original implementation.

issues.title: Empty suffix array incorrectly bypasses generic calendar filtering
issues.description: The filtering logic adds a length check (genericCalendarSuffixes?.length) that treats an empty array as falsy, setting AND to undefined instead of an empty array. In Prisma, AND: undefined means no filtering, while AND: [] also means no filtering but with different semantics. More critically, this breaks the filtering for providers like office365_calendar that have an empty suffix list in GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES. The double optional chaining (?. used twice) is redundant and the length check changes the behavior from the intended design where empty arrays should still be processed.

issues.title: Incomplete class rename breaks all imports and causes runtime failures
issues.description: The class was renamed from SelectedCalendarRepository to PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository (line 5) without providing a backward-compatible export alias. This breaks all existing code that imports this class. The test file within this PR (SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts:2,50,53) still imports and instantiates the old class name, causing test failures. Production code in apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts:41 and apps/web/app/api/webhooks/calendar-subscription/[provider]/route.ts:61 also use 'new SelectedCalendarRepository(prisma)' which will fail at runtime with a TypeError indicating SelectedCalendarRepository is not a constructor.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26774 - feat: CalendarCache - filter generic calendars from subscription batch

structured_output.summary:
The PR excludes Google's generic calendars (holiday, group, import, resource) from the calendar-subscription batch. A `GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES` constant feeds a new `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` on the adapter factory. `CalendarSubscriptionService.checkForNewSubscriptions` passes those suffixes into `findNextSubscriptionBatch`, which adds one `NOT endsWith` clause per suffix in Prisma. The filtering approach is sound: it happens in SQL before `take: 100`, so generic calendars don't eat batch slots.

The PR as written breaks production. It renames the exported class in `SelectedCalendarRepository.ts` from `SelectedCalendarRepository` to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository`, but two API routes still import and instantiate the old name. Those routes will throw at runtime, and the repository's own test file will fail to load. The remaining issues are test quality: the new `AND: undefined` assertions pass vacuously, and `getGenericCalendarSuffixes` has no unit test.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The class rename is a hard blocker. `apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts` and `apps/web/app/api/webhooks/calendar-subscription/[provider]/route.ts` still do `import { SelectedCalendarRepository } from ".../selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository"` and `new SelectedCalendarRepository(prisma)`. That export no longer exists, so the cron job and the webhook path fail. The repository test file also imports the old name and fails to load. The filter logic itself is reasonable, but the rename needs to be reverted or the callers updated before merge.

architecture.overview:
Calendar subscriptions are driven by `CalendarSubscriptionService`. Two entry points construct it: the cron route `apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts` and the webhook route `apps/web/app/api/webhooks/calendar-subscription/[provider]/route.ts`. Both inject a `SelectedCalendarRepository` built on Prisma. `checkForNewSubscriptions` asks the repository for up to 100 `SelectedCalendar` rows that are unsubscribed or whose channel has expired, limited to users in teams with the cache feature flag, and then subscribes each row through the provider adapter.

This PR adds a second filter to that query. `GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES` in `AdaptersFactory.ts` lists Google's generic calendar suffixes. The factory flattens them through the new `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()`, and the service passes them down. The repository turns each suffix into a `NOT: { externalId: { endsWith } }` clause inside `AND`. Because the filter runs in SQL before `take`, generic calendars never occupy batch slots. The PR also renames the repository class, and that rename is where the breakage comes from.
steps: Entry points: the cron and webhook routes create `new SelectedCalendarRepository(prisma)` and pass it into `CalendarSubscriptionService`. Both routes are unchanged by this PR, but they depend on the class name.
Service: `checkForNewSubscriptions` now calls `adapterFactory.getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` and forwards the result to `findNextSubscriptionBatch`.
Factory: `AdaptersFactory.ts` owns the per-provider suffix map and returns the flattened list through the new interface method. Office 365 contributes an empty list.
Repository: `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository.findNextSubscriptionBatch` adds an `AND` array of negated `endsWith` clauses. The class rename here is the part that breaks the callers.
Tests: the service and repository tests were updated to assert the new argument and where clause. The factory test was not updated.

findings.title: Class rename breaks production callers and the repository test file
findings.body:
`SelectedCalendarRepository` was renamed to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository` in `SelectedCalendarRepository.ts`, but the export was not preserved and the callers were not updated.

::diff{file="packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.ts" lines="5-5"}

The following still import the old name from that path:
- `apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts` (line 11, instantiated at line 41)
- `apps/web/app/api/webhooks/calendar-subscription/[provider]/route.ts` (line 14, instantiated at line 61)
- `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts` (line 3, instantiated at line 53)

In the routes, `new SelectedCalendarRepository(prisma)` will fail at runtime, since the import resolves to `undefined`. That takes down the calendar subscription cron and the webhook path. The rename also isn't needed for this feature.

::callout{type="warning"}
The PR's own test file will fail to load for the same reason, so the test command in the PR description will not pass.

The simplest fix is to revert the rename and keep `export class SelectedCalendarRepository`. If the rename is kept, update all three importers.
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.ts` line 5, the class was renamed to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository`, which breaks existing imports. Revert the rename so the class is exported as `SelectedCalendarRepository` again. The implementation and the `genericCalendarSuffixes` change stay as they are. Then confirm that `apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts` and `apps/web/app/api/webhooks/calendar-subscription/[provider]/route.ts` still compile against the same import, and that `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts` loads. Do not change the constructor or the query.

findings.title: Factory test not updated for getGenericCalendarSuffixes
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/calendar-subscription/adapters/__tests__/AdaptersFactory.test.ts`, add a `describe("getGenericCalendarSuffixes")` block. Assert that `factory.getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` returns exactly the four Google suffixes from `GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES` in `AdaptersFactory.ts` (`@group.v.calendar.google.com`, `@group.calendar.google.com`, `@import.calendar.google.com`, `@resource.calendar.google.com`). Import the constant rather than copying the strings if you can. Follow the existing style of the file.

findings.title: Added `AND: undefined` assertions pass without checking anything
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts`, remove the `AND: undefined` lines added to the existing `findNextSubscriptionBatch` expectations, since they don't assert anything. Add two tests: one where `genericCalendarSuffixes` is `[]`, and one where it is omitted. Each should assert that the `findMany` call has no `AND` key (check that `where.AND` is undefined explicitly). Keep the existing style.

findings.title: Suffix filter is applied to every integration row, not scoped per provider
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/calendar-subscription/adapters/AdaptersFactory.ts`, `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` flattens all providers into one list. This is correct today, but it means a suffix for one provider would filter rows from another. Decide whether the filter should be scoped per integration. If yes, change the repository to build the `NOT` clauses per integration (for example `OR: [{ integration: 'google_calendar', NOT: ... }, ...]`), and change the interface accordingly. If no, leave the code as is and add a comment noting that the list is intentionally global.

findings.title: Minor cleanup in the suffix flatten and the repository ternary
findings.fixPrompt: Tidy two spots without changing behavior. In `packages/features/calendar-subscription/adapters/AdaptersFactory.ts` `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()`, replace the `Object.keys(...).flatMap(...)` with `Object.values(GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES).flat()`, which drops the cast. In `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.ts` around lines 41-45, drop the redundant `?.` before `.map` after the length check. Behavior should be identical.

findings.title: Generic suffix list and Prisma filter are a clean design
findings.body:
Pushing the filter into the Prisma `where` clause, instead of filtering in memory after the fetch, is the right call. Generic calendars are excluded before the `take: 100` limit, so they can't push real personal calendars out of a batch. The per-provider map also gives a clear place to add Office 365 entries later.

The service test checks that the suffix list is forwarded to the repository with the right arguments, and the repository test checks the exact `NOT`/`endsWith` shape. That's the right level for these layers.
